issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for the Course.instructor property: the problem statement and the template declare instructor as String, but the solution defines instructor as [String]. This cross-artifact inconsistency will confuse students about the expected type and how to supply instructor data when constructing a Course.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the instructor property type consistent across all artifacts. Either change the solution to use instructor: String (preferred to match the problem statement and template) and update any code that treats it as an array, or update the problem statement and template to specify instructor: [String] and adjust examples accordingly.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch in the solution: Client constructs a Course using a String for the instructor parameter, but the Course initializer in the solution expects an [String]. This inner-solution inconsistency will cause compilation errors and prevents students from running the provided example.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Course initializer parameter with usage in Client and the problem statement. Change the solution's initializer signature to accept instructor: String and update internal storage to a String, or change the Client example to pass an array of strings. The simpler fix is to make the instructor parameter a String in the solution so it matches the template and problem examples.

issues.description: The concept 'instructor' is presented as a single String in the Problem Statement and in the Template (Course initializer and example usage), but the Solution implements Course.instructor as an array ([String]). Moreover the Solution's Client still passes a String literal when constructing a Course. This mismatch (same conceptual entity represented differently across artifacts) creates mapping confusion for students and produces a compile/type inconsistency between Course and its usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the 'instructor' concept consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) keep it as a single String (preferred minimal change) — change solution's Course.instructor and its initializer to type String and adjust any code that treats it as an array; or (B) make the problem statement, template examples, and Client show instructor as [String] and update the template and client code to pass an array. Ensure the initializer signatures and example usages match the chosen representation.
